description:
pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:147-243 — five of the eight Error variants wrap upstream error types as opaque payloads:

    pub enum Error {
        Path(pkix_path::Error),
        Revocation(pkix_revocation::Error),
        Identity(pkix_identity::IdentityError),
        Aia(pkix_aia::AiaError),
        PathBuild(pkix_path_builder::Error),
        // ... ProfileViolation, OcspDelegation, AiaDepthExceeded are local
    }

The slash-command checklist for leakage names this exact shape:

> Error types that wrap third-party error types in their public surface rather than mapping to a stable local enum.

WHY IT MATTERS — three concrete leakage consequences:

1. **Variant proliferation on upstream changes.** Every time pkix-path adds an error variant (e.g. `pkix_path::Error::Pq sig` for a future PQ algorithm), pkix-chain's surface area silently grows: a caller's `match error { Error::Path(pkix_path::Error::X) => ... }` matches expand. If the upstream is `#[non_exhaustive]` the new variant is non-breaking for SOFT match arms; if the caller patterns-matches inside `Error::Path(_)` exhaustively, it's breaking. The caller has no clean facade-layer abstraction to lean on.

2. **Display chain leakage.** pkix_chain::Error::Display produces "path validation: {pkix_path::Error::Display}". The caller's user-facing log line directly reflects pkix-path's wording choices. A future pkix-path refactor that improves error messages cascades through pkix-chain without pkix-chain having any input on the wording. A consumer who pinned pkix-chain's log format ("our service emits log lines like `path validation: chain broken at index 0`") is depending on a deep transitive contract.

3. **Source-chain depth.** `Error::source()` (lines 263-276) routes the source chain to the inner upstream error. A consumer using `std::error::Error::sources()` (the iterator added in 1.65) sees a fixed-depth chain whose shape depends on the upstream error's own source chain. If pkix-path wraps DER errors today and the source chain is `pkix_chain::Error -> pkix_path::Error -> der::Error`, but a future pkix-path refactor adds an intermediate -> `pkix_chain::Error -> pkix_path::Error -> pkix_path::InnerError -> der::Error`, the depth changes. Code doing `err.sources().nth(2)` to find the root cause silently changes meaning.

OPTIONS:

(a) **Map upstream errors to a local taxonomy.** Replace `Error::Path(pkix_path::Error)` with rich local variants: `Error::ChainBroken { index: usize }`, `Error::ExpiredCertificate { index: usize }`, `Error::SignatureInvalid { index: usize }`, `Error::TrustAnchorMismatch`, ... The mapping function lives in pkix-chain and can be evolved independently of the upstreams. Loses the source-chain link to the upstream's structured error but gains pkix-chain control of the surface. This is the slash-command checklist's recommended shape.

(b) **Carry upstream Error as Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync> behind an opaque local Diagnostic type.** Keep the source() chain (callers can downcast if they want to) but don't expose `pkix_path::Error` as part of pkix-chain's match-able surface. Local variants describe pkix-chain semantics; the inner Box is debug-only.

(c) **Status quo: document the leakage.** Add a Stability note ("Error::Path's inner variant set follows pkix-path's enum; changes to pkix-path errors are transitively breaking for pkix-chain match arms"). Acknowledges what consumers are signing up for. Same shape as PKIX-sqek.25's option (c) for the module re-export lock-in.

The PKIX-sqek.1 finding (slow-path validity errors surface as PathBuild instead of Path(ValidityPeriod)) is the FIRST concrete cost of this leakage: callers writing `match err { Error::Path(pkix_path::Error::ValidityPeriod{..}) => "leaf expired" }` get DIFFERENT variant routing depending on whether the chain hit the fast or slow path. A local taxonomy (option a) would have a single `Error::ExpiredCertificate { index }` variant either way. The leakage is what's enabling the inconsistency PKIX-sqek.1 captures.

PRE-1.0 FRAMING: a major redesign of the Error type is free pre-1.0. Picking (a) requires authoring the mapping; (b) is the minimum-effort path that still removes the lock-in. Both are non-breaking after 1.0 only if Error stays `#[non_exhaustive]` (it is, line 149). The lock-in is on the inner-variant taxonomy, which `#[non_exhaustive]` does not cover at the upstream layer.

Filed as priority 1 because Error is the single most-touched type in any consumer's pkix-chain code, and this shape decision sets the maintenance cost for every error-handling change in any of five upstream crates.
title: Error enum wraps five upstream error types directly in public variants — transparent leakage of every upstream design decision
